language_context.national_language_note: Japanese is the predominant language of public life. The country's linguistic landscape also includes Indigenous Ainu and Ryukyuan languages, as well as regional varieties and community languages.
language_context.diversity_note: UNESCO's endangered-language references for Japan include Ainu and several Ryukyuan varieties, as well as Hachijo. Linguistic classification is contested in some cases; LWT records community and scholarly distinctions instead of automatically labelling all varieties as mere dialects. Profiles currently distinguish Hokkaido Ainu, Kunigami, Shuri Okinawan, Southern Amami-Oshima, Miyako, Yaeyama and Yonaguni. Hachijo remains uncoded pending current ISO verification. Hachijo now has a profile keyed internally by Glottocode hach1239; it remains without an ISO 639-3 identifier.
language_context.documentation_unit: Use individual language/community profiles. Keep Japanese regional dialects distinct from separate Ryukyuan languages where the cited linguistic source does so.

languages.name: Southern Amami-Oshima
regions: southern Amami-Oshima; Setouchi documented in the linked profile
languages.note: ISO 639-3 ams identifies Southern Amami-Oshima, not all Amami island varieties. Northern Amami-Oshima, Kikai, Tokunoshima, Okinoerabu and Yoron require separate scope/code verification.

languages.name: Hachijo
languages.note: Glottolog identifies Hachijo as hach1239. No ISO 639-3 identifier or BCP 47 language tag was confirmed; iso_639_3 remains null and no code is invented.
